notes: SOURCES. hunterirrigation.com / hunterindustries.com (product pages, their print/pdf pages and /sites/default/files/IC_I20_dom.pdf) refused every automated fetch (HTTP 403 from Hunter's CDN) and web.archive.org was unreachable, so every chart was read from Hunter's own documents as hosted by distributors: Hunter product-page prints generated by hunterindustries.com (PGP Ultra, SRM: Sep 2022; PGJ: Apr 2025), the Hunter domestic Product Catalog (Oct 2016), the Hunter SRM/PGJ Performance Card (LIT-379 D 10/20) and the Hunter PGP Product Information booklet (LIT-213 Rev E, 2008). Each family's source names the exact file. US-unit charts only; the metric charts were not used.

CROSS-CHECK. Every row was compared by script with a second Hunter document (PGP Ultra/I-20 2022 page vs 2016 catalogue; PGP 2016 catalogue vs 2008 booklet; PGJ 2025 page vs 2016 catalogue; SRM 2022 page vs 2020 performance card) and every row's square precip was checked against 96.25 x gpm x 2 / radius^2. The only disagreements are the ones listed in these notes.

PRECIP BASIS. Hunter's footnote on every rotor chart: 'All precipitation rates calculated for 180 degree operation. For the precipitation rate for a 360 degree sprinkler, divide by 2.' So chartPrecip for a rotor nozzle is the figure for a HALF-circle head; a full-circle head with the same nozzle gives half. chartPrecip carries two keys beyond SCHEMA.md: 'psi' (the chart's bold 'recommended pressure' row the figures come from) and 'arcDeg' (180, the arc they are calculated for). Hunter prints precip at every pressure; only the recommended row is kept.

RECOMMENDED PRESSURE (the bold rows, read from the font weight of the 2016 catalogue and the 2025 PGJ page): blue standard 45 psi; grey low-angle 50; black short-radius 50; green high-flow 10, 13 and 8.0 LA 60, 6.0 LA 50; original-PGP red 50, original-PGP gray low-angle 50 (10LA 60); PGJ and SRM 40. The 2022 PGP Ultra page's faux-bold rendering appears to bold 13 and 8.0 LA at 50 psi instead; that rendering is unreliable and the 2016 bolding was used.

MPR ROTOR NOZZLES (hu-pgpu-mpr25/30/35). Fixed-arc matched-precipitation nozzles for the PGP Ultra / I-20 rotor: flow 'constant', gpm AS PRINTED for the nozzle at its own arc (NOT a full-circle equivalent; e.g. MPR-25-Q at 25 psi = 0.74 gpm), arcFixed set, arcMin/arcMax null; the rotor's arc must be set to match. Flows are not proportional to the arc (Q x 4 = 2.96 gpm vs F = 2.78 gpm at 25 psi), which is another reason they are kept per arc. Their printed precip is for their own arc and no row is bolded, so chartPrecip is null.

MPR 360-degree (F) rows at 65 psi: the 2022 page stops at 55 psi for all three F nozzles. The 2016 catalogue prints a 65 psi row for MPR-25-F (25 ft, 4.63 gpm) and MPR-35-F (35 ft, 9.18 gpm); those two rows are included from it (their families' source says so). MPR-30-F has no 65 psi row in either document.

BLUE 2.0 AT 65 PSI: the current PGP Ultra / I-20 chart (2022 page) prints 34 ft, 2.3 gpm, 0.38/0.44; the 2016 catalogue and the 2008 PGP booklet print 32 ft, 2.3 gpm, 0.43/0.50 (each internally consistent). hu-pgpu-blue uses the 2022 value (34 ft); hu-pgp-blue (the original-PGP chart) keeps 32 ft. Every other blue row is identical between the two.

TRAJECTORY: 25 degrees for blue and red standard nozzles, 13 degrees for grey/gray low-angle, as the spec lines state. No trajectory is given for the green high-flow nozzles (including 6.0 LA and 8.0 LA, which are presumably low-angle but not stated) or the black short-radius nozzles: null. PGJ and SRM: Hunter says '14 degrees approximately'.

ARC: PGP Ultra and I-20 (and their PRB bodies) adjust 50-360; PGJ and SRM 40-360; the original PGP-ADJ 40-360. PGP-360 is a full-circle-only body that takes the same nozzles, but the schema keeps the arc on the nozzle and those nozzles say 40-360: treat a PGP-360 head as 360 degrees.

PGP ULTRA AND I-20 take the same nozzles (every Hunter chart is titled 'PGP Ultra / I-20'). The pressure-regulated bodies (PGP-04-PRB, I-20-04/06-PRB, I-20-04/06-SS-PRB, regulated to 45 psi at the nozzle, inlet 55-100 psi) are from the 2016 catalogue, which lists blue, grey, black and MPR nozzles for them but not green high-flow; they are not on the 2022 page, so whether they are still sold was not confirmed.

'I-20 ULTRA': no separate US product was found. The name appears on a 2015 Hunter brochure for New Zealand describing the same I-20 (50-360 arc, same nozzle racks, though it lists 'MPR-20' where US documents list MPR-25 -- not transcribed). Treat an 'I-20 Ultra' as the hu-i20-* bodies.

ORIGINAL PGP (pre-Ultra, PGP-ADJ / PGP-360): red #1-#12, blue 1.5-8.0 and gray low-angle #4LA-#10LA from the 2016 catalogue's PGP page, cross-checked against the 2008 booklet. One disagreement: red #5 at 30 psi is 32 ft, 1.6 gpm (0.30/0.35) in 2016 but 34 ft, 1.6 gpm (0.27/0.31) in 2008; the 2016 value is used. The 2008 booklet labels the gray nozzles 4-10 without 'LA'. The old gray numbering is not the Ultra numbering (old 5LA, 6LA, 7LA rows equal Ultra 2.0LA, 2.5LA, 3.5LA; old 8LA is not 4.5LA). The shrub (PGS) and 12-inch (PGH) versions of the original PGP were not added. PGP-360 appears only in the 2008 booklet.

SRM: the current 8-nozzle SRM (.50-4.0, dark green) from the 2022 page, identical to the 2020 performance card. The 2016 catalogue shows an older 6-nozzle SRM chart (.50-3.0, 18 degree trajectory, longer radii, e.g. 3.0 at 40 psi = 30 ft) whose .75 rows repeat the .50 rows exactly, apparently a misprint; it was NOT transcribed. An older SRM may carry that older nozzle set. SRM 1.0 at 40 psi prints 19 ft, 1.0 gpm with precip 0.51/0.59, a little below what 1.0 gpm at 19 ft gives (0.53); transcribed as printed.

PGJ: the 2025 page's header says 'Radius 15-34 ft, Flow 0.42-4.3 GPM' (the SRM's figures), but its chart runs .75-5.0 to 37 ft and 5.3 gpm; the chart was used, and it is identical to the 2016 catalogue's. PGJ (red .75-5.0) and SRM (dark green .50-4.0) are separate nozzle sets with near-identical rows where they overlap (e.g. 4.0 at 40 psi: 34 ft PGJ, 33 ft SRM).

Hunter's chart notes (2008 PGP booklet): data are test results in zero wind; the radius may be reduced up to 25% with the adjustment screw, so rows are for an unreduced nozzle. Shrub-riser models (PGP-00, I-20-00, PGJ-00) have popUpIn null.
